Real Life Inspirations?  Speculations about what inspired George. [Spoilers MAIN]

Ashara Dayne inspired by Elizabeth Taylor.  GRRM was enamoured with the film Ivanhoe and put elements of it in the lore, as evidenced by the Tourney of Ashford.  Elizabeth Taylor is famous for her beauty and her violet eyes and starred as one of the main ladies in Ivanhoe.

Lyanna Stark inspired by Joan Baez.  Long, beautiful face.  Social justice advocates.  (Lyanna's becoming Knight of the Laughing Tree during the tourney and Joan Baez's own advocacy.  One could even say that their faith plays a role for both.  The Laughing Tree is a weirwood; Joan Baez is a Quaker.)  Like Joan, Lyanna runs off with a married singer.  (Not that I equate Bob Dylan with Rhaegar.)

The years in the current series were originally intended to parallel those in real life.  The first 3 books came out in 96, 98, and 99.  The book series began in 298.  GRRM tried to implement a year jump in Feast, which was published in 2005.

[Spoilers EXTENDED] Why didn't Edmure escape with the Blackfish while surrendering Riverrun?

Towards the end of AFFC, we learn that Jaime sends Edmure inside Riverrun, and then Edmure takes a whole day to surrender the castle, before which the Blackfish as escaped by swimming across the river floating quietly downstream. Jaime doesn't find out the Blackfish is missing till the next morning after the castle gates are opened. If one man could escape, why not two? That couldn't be too difficult, if an old man was able to manage it. Also, before sending him into Riverrun, Jaime leaves Edmure alone with the singer Tom of Sevenstreams for a while, and there are popular fan theories that Tom is an agent working for the BWB. Maybe he told Edmure about some rescue plans? 

And then Edmure went inside Riverrun and told the Blackfish about it, and since they took so long to strike the Direwolf banners and open the gates, they both could have escaped together? Did both of them decide that it was important for their plan for Edmure to assume his captivity for now, but the Blackfish must escape to gather his forces with the BWB, or even ride to the Vale to obtain help from the Vale lords?

(SPOILERS MAIN) Is it plausible Pycelle was poisoning Elia's womb?

Pycelle is loyal as fuck to Tywin. I think that's because he's a son of Rohanne and Eustace Osgrey (because otherwise Jason Lannister (Tytos' brother) would be Lord Webber, and so his kids wouldn't be at Casterly Rock for Tywin to fall in love with Joanna). 

But anyways, that's neither here or there.

So when Elia was named Queen, Tywin was obviously spiteful. Now Rhaegar probably moved with Elia to Dragonstone because he didn't trust Pycelle. But Elia was weak and feeble, and needed to go to King's Landing, before going to Harrenhal for the wedding. 

So Pycelle, at a "routine" check-up, envious that Tywin had just fled King's Landing, could have easily poisoned Elia's womb, which caused Aegon to be born so traumatically, which meant Rhaegar needed Lyanna for his prophecy baby Visenya.

  
So Pycelle may have actually started Robert's Rebellion, and the War of the Five Kings, however indirectly.

>"Not now," she agreed. "One day. One day you must tell me all. The good and the bad. There is some good to be said of my father, surely?"

>"There is, Your Grace. Of him, and those who came before him. Your grandfather Jaehaerys and his brother, their father Aegon, your mother . . . and Rhaegar. Him most of all." - Daenerys VI, A Storm of Swords

Curiously, Barristan only mentions one brother even though Jaehaerys had two, Duncan and Daeron.

Cat does think of Jenny and Duncan when she passes through Oldstones so we know for a fact Duncan was invented already in ASOS.

At first, I was thinking it's most likely Daeron Barristan thinks of since he was a warrior who died quelling a rebellion while Duncan the Small was a useless guy who started another rebellion. But then this whole passage is about the "good and bad" of the family which still includes Duncan and his vices. Or it's possible Barristan just doesn't think Duncan is worth talking about.

If you switch out Jaime for another member of the Kingsguard the day KL got sacked, do you think they make the same decision? [Spoilers EXTENDED]

Basically as the title implies. I know the fandom jokes about Barristan “the Bystander” and “Fraud of the Morning” and all that. But really think, if Barristan Selmy was in the throne room that day and Aerys tells him he’s gonna burn down the city, do you think he lets it happen? I mean this is an entire city of people, could him or an Arthur Dayne live with that level of bloodshed? 

To be clear, this isn’t an attempt to minimize the courageous thing Jaime did. I’m just more curious how far the loyalty of a lot of the KG guys were, and if anyone thinks they would hit a breaking point similar to Jaime. Would they just kill the pyromancers and leave Aerys alive to be detained? Or would any of them follow their orders and allow the city to be blown up?

(Spoilers Main) Could any Starkaryen be TPTWP

GRRM said in an interview that Baelor's death at the Ashford tourney greatly changed the trajectory of Westeros. Which got me thinking, what if Baelor \*and his line\* survived.

\- We get King Baelor, who (also according to GRRM) would be a good ruler. The crown then passes to his grand/son in this fictional scenario. No important Targaryens die in the plague ;)

\- We do NOT get the tragedy at Summerhall, as Prince Egg wouldn't have the same resources as King Aegon V to pull that one off

\- We do NOT get Mad King Aerys II

Imagine it's 281 AC and a stronger, more beloved Targaryen holds the throne. Prince Daeron falls in love with Lyanna Stark at the tourney at Harrenhall.

Do we still get the Prince That Was Promised? Does it \*have\* to be Rhaegar x Lyanna, or could any Starkaryen fit the bill?
